hook.text: Anything that moves has kinetic energy—from a speeding truck to a drifting molecule of air.

buildup.text: Kinetic energy equals half the mass times velocity squared—double your speed and you quadruple your energy.

discovery.text: That's why car crashes at 60 mph are four times more destructive than at 30 mph—speed matters exponentially.

twist.text: Even sitting still, your molecules are vibrating—thermal energy is just kinetic energy at the atomic scale.

climax.text: The fastest human-made object is the Parker Solar Probe at 635,000 km/h—kinetic energy equals 10 tons of TNT.

punchline.text: Speed squared—that's why fast things hit so hard.

quiz.question: What happens to kinetic energy when speed doubles?
